subject: Clarify anchored rate guard, caps/floors and carveout language
messages:
From: Susan Moretti <susan.moretti@brightgrid.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-28T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on pricing schedule caps/floors + carveouts

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for sending over the draft order form. We reviewed Exhibit B (pricing schedule) and have a few substantive questions before we can move to redlines:

1) Clause 3.2 (Fee Collar / Floor) — the draft references an "anchored rate guard" but doesn't define the base measurement period. Can you confirm whether the floor/collar is measured quarterly or annually, and whether it uses billed tokens or invoiced usage?

2) Clause 3.5 (Carveouts) — there is a carveout for "sandbox & R&D" that is currently worded as "non-production usage excluded where reasonably identified." That is too vague for our procurement/legal teams. We need an explicit threshold or a tagging requirement (e.g., project tag + environment flag) to operationalize the carveout in billing.

3) Clause 4.1 (Caps) — the cap language appears to allow an automatic overage rate step-up after X% variance. BrightGrid needs an explicit cap on the maximum effective rate increase in any given 30-day window.

4) True-up timing: the draft is silent on whether true-ups happen on calendar quarter or at contract anniversary. Which is Redwood's standard?

I've attached our initial questions and a short table of proposed redline bullets. Could we get Redwood's suggested operative language for the carveout (we prefer a tagging + monthly audit approach) and confirm the floor/collar measurement period?

We're happy to take a 30-minute call this week if that's easier.

Regards,
Susan Moretti
Director, Procurement
BrightGrid Health
Attachment: BrightGrid_init_questions_20260628.pdf
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Moretti <susan.moretti@brightgrid.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on pricing schedule caps/floors + carveouts

Hi Susan — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then attached is a more formal proposed redline from our side: RI_proposed_exhibit_B_redline_20260629.pdf.

- Measurement period: Redwood measures the floor/collar on billed usage aggregated monthly with a quarterly true-up by default; we can agree to an annual reconciliation if you prefer. We'll note the measurement uses billed tokens (post-credits).

- Carveout operationalization: We can accept a tagging requirement, provided BrightGrid commits to a monthly export that includes the project/environment tag. Our billing team will only exclude usage where the tag matches the agreed pattern (e.g., tag prefix BG-RD- or environment:development/test).

- Cap on rate increases: We can cap any step increase to a maximum of X% (we suggest 20%) in a 30-day window; see proposed redline for exact phrasing.

Next steps: I've looped in Karthik for commercial fallback and Laura + Rishi from Legal to confirm the language is supportable. If you can review our PDF redline and send a counter-redline, we can get this to a final position quickly. Happy to do a 30-min sync — Karthik, please surface available slots.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: BrightGrid Legal <contracts@brightgrid.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Susan Moretti <susan.moretti@brightgrid.com>
Date: 2026-06-29T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Questions on pricing schedule caps/floors + carveouts — counter redline

Hi Sofia,

We reviewed Redwood's proposed redline and submitted a tracked-changes version with comments. Key open items:

- We pushed back on the quarterly true-up (we prefer calendar-quarter true-up tied to invoice cycles rather than an annual reconciliation).
- The tagging operationalization is acceptable, but we requested a fallback audit process if tags are missing (we proposed a 7-day remediation window and then rollback to billed usage if unresolved).
- Rate increase cap: we proposed a lower ceiling (12% per 30-day window) and asked for a formula showing example calculations for typical usage profiles.

Attached: BrightGrid_counter_redline_20260629.docx (comments inline).

Please propose a single-winner position by EOD tomorrow so we can present to our CFO.

Thanks,
BrightGrid Contracts
Attachment: BrightGrid_counter_redline_20260629.docx
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: BrightGrid Contracts <contracts@brightgrid.com>, Susan Moretti <susan.moretti@brightgrid.com>

Date: 2026-06-29T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on pricing schedule caps/floors + carveouts — internal review + recommendation

Internal thread (reply-all with our recommended approach) — posting the short recommended negotiation plan so BG has clarity by EOD:

Karthik / Laura / Rishi — summary of BrightGrid asks and our recommended position:

1) True-up cadence
- BG prefers calendar-quarter true-ups; commercial impact vs. our standard quarterly (billed monthly, quarterly true-up) is neutral. Recommend we accept BG's calendar-quarter phrasing for clarity (win).

2) Tagging + fallback audit
- We can accept project/environment tagging as the primary exclusion mechanism. Proposed operational fallback: if tags missing for >0.5% of monthly usage or if a given tag is disputed, BrightGrid has 7 days to remediate. If unresolved, usage will be invoiced and credited in the following quarter subject to audit findings. Rishi: are we comfortable with the 0.5% tolerance threshold?

3) Rate increase cap
- BG asked for 12% ceiling; we proposed 20%. Commercial preference is to split the difference at 15% to close quickly. Karthik: recommend we offer 15% per 30-day window with a carveout that for predictable burst events (scheduled load tests, migrations) the parties can pre-notify to avoid bracketed step-ups.

4) Example math and transparency
- Laura: please produce a one-page annex with two worked examples (steady-state and burst profile) showing the collar/floor math and the application of the cap — that will help the CFO.

5) Final mechanics
- Acceptance path: we send revised redline (legal + commercial changes) and request a single marked-up doc returned. If BG accepts 15% cap and calendar-quarter true-ups and the tagging fallback, we can mark as agreed and schedule DocuSign.

Action owners: Rishi to sign off on tagging tolerance wording by EOD; Laura to draft annex examples; Karthik to confirm commercial ok on 15% concession.

--
Sofia
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Susan Moretti <susan.moretti@brightgrid.com>, BrightGrid Contracts <contracts@brightgrid.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-30T16:45:00-07:00
Subject: Final proposed exhibit language and next steps (Exhibit B)

Hi Susan / BrightGrid team — thanks for the quick review and the counter-redline. Per our internal alignment, attached is Redwood's final proposed redline (RI_final_exhibit_B_redline_20260630.pdf) that implements the following agreed positions:

• True-up cadence: calendar-quarter true-ups tied to invoice cycles (explicitly stated).
• Carveout operationalization: project tag + environment flag required (example tags: BG-RD-*, env:dev/test). If >0.5% of monthly usage is untagged or disputed, BrightGrid will be given a 7-day remediation window; unresolved items will be invoiced and subject to quarter-end credit after audit.
• Rate increase cap: 15% maximum effective step-up in any 30-day window; scheduled maintenance/migration events may be pre-notified to avoid triggering the step-up.

We also included a short one-page annex with two worked examples showing how the collar/floor math and cap apply to a steady-state and a burst month. See page 3 of the attached PDF.

Next steps: please review the attached and, if acceptable, return a single tracked-change document or confirm via email so we can prepare DocuSign. If you'd prefer a call, I have 09:00–11:00 PT tomorrow and can gap 30 minutes in the afternoon as well — Karthik will also join.

Thanks again — we think this approach balances predictability for BrightGrid while protecting the unit economics Redwood needs for predictable capacity.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Executive — Enterprise
